evidence: task/task.toml [environment] contains exactly four keys: `build_timeout_sec = 600.0`, `network_mode = "public"`, `cpus = 2`, `memory_mb = 4096`. Parsed with tomllib: {'build_timeout_sec': 600.0, 'network_mode': 'public', 'cpus': 2, 'memory_mb': 4096}; a recursive walk of the whole parsed document finds no key containing 'image' in any table ([verifier.environment] holds only network_mode). A case-insensitive grep for `docker_image` and for compose files across the non-solution task tree returns nothing, so no alternative mechanism names a prebuilt image. The agent Dockerfile task/environment/Dockerfile has active build steps (line 1 `FROM node:22-bookworm-slim`; lines 5-7 apt install; lines 9-12 `npm install -g ... express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1`; lines 14-15 `COPY instructions/ /instructions/` and `COPY assets/ /assets/`; lines 16-23 git init of /app) and is byte-identical (cmp) to the frozen template environment/Dockerfile; the [environment] block is also identical to the template's. Since docker_image is absent, the Dockerfile is the build source and is not dead code, which is what the workbook row, quality-checks.md check 12 (`[environment].docker_image is not set while the agent Dockerfile still has active build steps`) and staged-task-contract.md line 78 require. Adversarial variants considered: docker_image under a differently cased or nested table, in [verifier.environment], or commented in and out - none present. This row is a static configuration property fully determined by the frozen bytes; no runtime measurement is required for it. I did not read a harbor build log for these exact bytes, so the run verdict is NOT EXERCISED (the indexed hosted run is on an earlier candidate and the scripted golden is not a harbor environment build).
